description.content: Use this REST API for managing and monitoring firewall features, including metrics, repository management, quarantine operations, and namespace confusion prevention.

Use this method to retrieve the details of components that are auto-released from quarantine.

Permissions required: View IQ Elements

query.description: Enter the number of results to be returned for a page.
Enter the `policyId`. When provided, the results will include the components that have a policy violation for the policyId.
Enter the component name. When provided, the results will include components with display names (case-insensitive) that match the given name.
Select `true` to set the sort order to ascending.

response.name:
The response includes:
  • `total` is the total number of records this request can return across all pages.
  • `page` is the page number specified in the request.
  • `pageSize` is the page size specified in the request.
  • `pageCount` is the total number of pages this request can return.
The `results` section contains details of each component that has been auto-released. It includes:
  • `displayName` is the name and version of the component.
  • `repository` indicates the repository name where the component is stored.
  • `quarantineDate` is the date and time when the component was quarantined.
  • `dateCleared` is the date and time when the component was auto-released from quarantine.
  • `quarantinePolicyViolations` will be empty for components that are auto-released.
  • `componentIdentifier` is the format and coordinates for the component.
  • `pathname` indicates the component path in the repository.
  • `hash` is the hash of the component.
  • `matchState` indicates the whether the component is an `EXACT` or `SIMILAR` match to the known components or is `UNKNOWN`.
  • `repositoryId` is the ID of the repository where the component is stored.
  • `quarantined` indicates whether the component is quarantined.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: basic

Use this method to evaluate components (max. 100).

**Hash Requirements by Format Type:**

**Coordinate-Based Formats** (hash NOT required when using packageUrl):
- golang, conan, cargo, cocoapods, cran, conda, composer, hf-model
- These formats identify components by coordinates (name+version) rather than file hash
- When using packageUrl, hash is optional
- If hash is provided, it will be used

**Hash-Based Formats** (hash REQUIRED):
- maven, npm, pypi, nuget, docker, rubygems, and others
- Hash must ALWAYS be provided to identify the exact file content
- Hash is required regardless of whether pathname or packageUrl is used
- Missing hash for these formats will result in incorrect component identification

Permissions required: Evaluate Individual Components

response.name: The response contains the evaluation results.

This operation asynchronously re-evaluates the specified component across all repositories where the component exists.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: basic

Get the status of a cascade re-evaluation request.

Returns the current progress of a cascade re-evaluation operation including the list of components that have been evaluated and those still pending. The overall status will be 'pending' if any components are still being processed, or 'completed' if all components have been evaluated.

The response includes:

  • status: Overall status (PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, NO_COMPONENTS_FOUND, FAILED)
  • referenceComponentHash: The component hash that was re-evaluated
  • pending: Components still being processed (PENDING status)
  • evaluated: Components successfully re-evaluated (COMPLETED or NO_COMPONENTS_FOUND status)
  • failed: Components that could not be re-evaluated (FAILED status)

Permissions Required: Evaluate Components at Repository Managers level
